title: Wgpu Renderer Note Canvas Parity
description: Implement the note-canvas componentScene surface in the wgpu renderer (framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs), which currently falls through to a placeholder. Port geometry/interaction logic from framework/renderer/react/components/note-canvas-host.tsx (block bounds/hit-testing, resize handles, screen<->world conversion, ink erasers, snap-to-grid, marquee selection) into a direct DrawList painter (render_note_canvas) following the render_canvas_2d/render_raster pattern, wired into SceneSurfaceState pointer handling. Verify against the `note` playground comparing wgpu vs react renderers.
summary:
Fixed 4 dock:: tests in framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs that failed on real logic after a prior session fixed their compile errors. All 16 lib tests now pass (`cargo test -p semio-framework-renderer-wgpu --lib`).

1. reorder_tab (lib.rs:330): removed the internal `to.saturating_sub(1)` pre-op-index adjustment. Cross-checked against the canonical TS reference (ui/js/react/index.tsx reorderTabInStack + applyModeDrop), which uses plain splice semantics — `to` is the final index in the post-removal list, with only a clamp, no subtraction. apply_drop already passed the raw index straight through, so only reorder_tab needed the fix.

2. split_axis_extent test (lib.rs ~1719): the test called `split_axis_extent(&vec![], canvas)` twice with the same path but asserted two different results (1000.0 then 800.0) — impossible for a pure function. Manually traced solve_node_bounds/split_axis_extent and confirmed the implementation is correct (Column->height, Row->width, recursion correct); fixed the test's first call to use `&vec![0]` (the nested Row) instead of `&vec![]` (root Column).

3 & 4. stack_content_rect (lib.rs:1468): removed a stray `.inset(theme.padding_standard)` that shrank every per-window body rect on all sides. This single bug caused both remaining failures: adjacent stacks in a row no longer touched (row_layout_stack_content_rects_match_per_window), and a maximized stack's body no longer filled the canvas (maximized_stack_uses_full_canvas_bounds). The returned rect is used for hit-testing, drop-zone splits, and measure-rail placement, not just visual content — it must be the exact geometric boundary; UiNode trees apply their own declarative padding internally via render_ui_node, so the outer inset was redundant double-padding. Left the separate inset in render_stack's inline paint path (lib.rs:1399) untouched — that's a distinct cosmetic fallback-draw path unrelated to the layout math under test.
